questions.question: If an applicant fails to submit the requisite application fee, the recruitment portal ___ the registration automatically.
questions.explanation: Ye ek automatic procedural rule aur general factual outcome hai. Zero Conditional formula: 'If + Simple Present, Simple Present'. Portal ka reject karna ek permanent administrative setup hai, isliye Simple Present 'rejects' (A) sahi answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Established rules aur automatic cause-and-effect processes mein dono clauses Simple Present mein rehte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the meteorological center forecasts heavy rainfall tomorrow, the judicial academy ___ the outdoor convocation ceremony.
questions.explanation: If-clause Simple Present ('forecasts') mein hai aur future realistic event ('tomorrow') ke liye condition rakhta hai. First Conditional ke mutabiq result clause 'will + V1' leta hai: 'will postpone' (B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Realistic future possibility ke liye First Conditional formula: 'If + Simple Present, will + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: The Registrar will issue the certified judgment copy if the counsel ___ the urgent processing fee today.
questions.explanation: Main clause 'will issue' hai. Subordinate conditional if-clause sentence ke baad mein aaya hai. Rule ke mutabiq if-clause mein future time ke liye bhi Simple Present lagta hai, 'will' nahi. 3rd person singular subject 'the counsel' ke sath 'pays' (B) correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Main clause pehle aane par bhi if-clause ke grammatical constraints wahi rehte hain: Simple Present (V1/V_s/es) use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the system administrator had the source code of the proprietary software, he ___ the security vulnerability immediately.
questions.explanation: If-clause Simple Past verb 'had' (possession) use kar raha hai, jo present hypothetical situation batata hai (reality ye hai ki uske paas source code nahi hai). Second Conditional rule ke mutabiq result clause mein 'would + V1' lagta hai: 'would patch' (B). Dhyan rahe, yahan 'had' main verb hai (Simple Past), auxiliary Past Perfect nahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Present hypothetical state (Simple Past V2 'had') ke sath result clause mein 'would + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If she ___ aware of the High Court's strict dress code, she would not wear informal attire to the courtroom.
questions.explanation: Result clause 'would not wear' (would + V1) Second Conditional ko mark karta hai. Present imaginary state ke liye formal English mein singular subject 'she' ke sath bhi subjunctive 'were' (C) use hota hai. 'Was' (B) exam standard par incorrect distractor hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Formal contrary-to-fact conditions mein sabhi persons ke sath subjunctive 'were' use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the vigilance wing had investigated the anonymous complaint properly, they ___ the financial embezzlement months ago.
questions.explanation: If-clause Past Perfect ('had investigated') mein hai aur past unfulfilled action batata hai. Third Conditional formula: 'If + had + V3, would have + V3'. Isliye result clause mein 'would have discovered' (C) sahi answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Unreal past conditions demand 'would have + V3' in the main result clause.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence containing a grammatical ERROR:

'If the court bailiff (A) / would have served the summons (B) / on the respondent earlier, (C) / the hearing would not have been adjourned. (D)'

options.text: the hearing would not have been adjourned.

questions.explanation: Part B mein grammatical error hai. Subordinate conditional if-clause ke andar 'would have' lagana bilkul galat hai. Yahan Third Conditional rule ke mutabiq Past Perfect 'had served' aana chahiye: 'If the court bailiff had served the summons...'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule PIT-01: 'Would' ya 'would have' kabhi bhi if-clause ke andar use nahi hota. Replace with 'had + V3'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Had the judicial magistrate ___ the confessional statement under Section 164 CrPC, it would have been admissible as primary evidence.
questions.explanation: Sentence 'Had' se shuru hone wali Type 3 formal inversion hai ('Had + Subject + V3'). Auxiliary 'Had' already subject se pehle aa chuka hai, isliye blank mein main verb ka past participle V3 'recorded' (B) aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'Had + Subject + V3 ..., would have + V3'. Inverted clause requires past participle (V3).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Were the state government ___ the sanctioned strength of judicial officers, the pending case burden would diminish rapidly.
questions.explanation: Type 2 conditional mein jab action verb ko 'Were' ke sath invert kiya jata hai, toh structure banta hai: 'Were + Subject + to + V1 ..., would + V1'. Isliye 'to increase' (B) grammatically correct hai. 'Increased' (C) ya 'increase' (A) galat hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Action verb inversion with Were follows: 'Were + Subject + to + V1 ..., would + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: ___ the network switch fail during court proceedings, the backup generator will activate immediately.
questions.explanation: Result clause 'will activate' (will + V1) First Conditional structure hai. First Conditional ki formal inversion 'Should + Subject + V1' hoti hai ('Should the network switch fail...'). 'Had' Type 3 ke liye hota hai aur 'Were' Type 2 ke liye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'Should + Subject + V1 ..., will + V1' formal Type 1 inversion express karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the accounts clerk had audited the ledgers last quarter, the financial discrepancy ___ not exist today.
questions.explanation: Sentence Mixed Conditional hai: Condition past ki unfulfilled action hai ('had audited last quarter'), lekin result present time ('today') ka state describe kar raha hai. Result mein present base verb 'exist' hai, isliye modal 'would' (B) aayega ('would not exist today'). 'Would have' ke baad V3 'existed' hona chahiye tha jo yahan nahi hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Mixed Conditional (Past Condition ➔ Present State): 'If + had + V3, would + V1 (today/now)'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: The applicant will be permitted to sit for the typing test, provided that he ___ the original admission card at the entry gate.
questions.explanation: 'Provided that' ek conditional connective hai jiska matlab 'on condition that' hota hai. Main clause 'will be permitted' First Conditional logic follow karta hai, isliye 'provided that' clause mein Simple Present verb 'displays' (B) aayega. Future marker 'will' (A) lagana galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: 'Provided that' clauses follow first conditional tense constraints (Simple Present for future conditions).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: As long as the interim injunction remains in force, the commercial developer ___ construction on the protected green belt.
questions.explanation: Condition clause Simple Present ('remains in force') mein continuing condition batata hai. Result clause mein present legal prohibition ko express karne ke liye present modal 'cannot resume' (A) perfectly suitable hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: 'As long as' expresses continuing condition with present modal concord.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.subtopic: Error Spotting: Double Negative with Unless
questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence with an ERROR:

'Unless the petitioner (A) / does not deposit the statutory cost (B) / within two weeks, (C) / the petition will stand dismissed. (D)'

options.text: does not deposit the statutory cost

questions.explanation: Part B mein error hai. 'Unless' already negative conjunction hai (Unless = If not). Iske sath 'does not' lagane se double negative banta hai. Sahi form hogi: 'Unless the petitioner deposits the statutory cost...'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule PIT-04: 'Unless' clause ke andar doosra negative particle (not, does not) use karna strictly prohibited hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Which of the following inverted sentences is grammatically CORRECT in word order?

options.text: Had not the high court intervened, the eviction would have proceeded.
Had the high court not intervened, the eviction would have proceeded.
Did the high court not intervened, the eviction would have proceeded.
Had the high court intervened not, the eviction would have proceeded.

questions.explanation: Option B perfectly standard negative inverted syntax ko follow karta hai: 'Had + Subject + not + V3'. Option A ('Had not the high court...') informal/galat word order hai. Option C auxiliary 'Did' ke sath V3 'intervened' laga raha hai jo double error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule PIT-05: Inverted negative syntax requires: 'Had + Subject + not + V3' (NOT 'Had not + Subject').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question:
Identify the conditional type of the following sentence:

'If the court registry were fully digitalized, judicial pendency would reduce by forty percent.'
questions.explanation: If-clause mein subjunctive 'were' (Simple Past hypothetical) hai aur result clause mein 'would + V1' ('would reduce') hai. Ye standard Second Conditional (Type 2) ka structure hai jo present contrary-to-fact situation ko represent karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: 'If + were / V2, would + V1' = Second Conditional (Type 2).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question:
Transform the following sentence into a formal inverted structure without changing its meaning:

'If the bench had delivered the ruling yesterday, the strike would have ended.'

options.text: Did the bench deliver the ruling yesterday, the strike would have ended.
Were the bench delivering the ruling yesterday, the strike would have ended.
Had the bench delivered the ruling yesterday, the strike would have ended.
Should the bench deliver the ruling yesterday, the strike would have ended.

questions.explanation: Original sentence Type 3 conditional ('If + had delivered, would have ended') mein hai. Type 3 conditional ko invert karne ke liye 'if' ko omit karke auxiliary 'Had' ko subject ke aage laya jata hai: 'Had the bench delivered...'. Isliye Option C bilkul exact transformation hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'If + Subject + had + V3' transforms into 'Had + Subject + V3'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If an advocate discovers an inadvertent misrepresentation in his pleading, he ___ inform the presiding judge at the earliest opportunity.
questions.explanation: If-clause Simple Present ('discovers') mein realistic future condition rakhta hai. Professional duty aur statutory mandate express karne ke liye First Conditional result clause mein modal 'must' (A) lagega ('must inform'). 'Would have' ya 'had' past counterfactuals ke liye aate hain jo present condition ke sath match nahi karte.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: First Conditional result clauses can use deontic obligation modals like 'must' or 'should'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the cyber forensic team had preserved the unencrypted hard drives, they ___ the ransomware origin.
questions.explanation: Condition clause Past Perfect ('had preserved') mein past unreal condition express karta hai. Result clause mein past hypothetical possibility ke liye 'might have + V3' ('might have traced') aayega. 'Might trace' (A) Type 2 present hypothetical ke liye use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Third Conditional speculative past possibility demands 'might have + V3'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Select the sentence that is grammatically ACCURATE in all respects:

options.text: If the chief engineer will inspect the server room, he will identify the overheating issue.
Unless the security guard does not check every badge, unauthorized visitors will enter.
Were the High Court to issue fresh recruitment guidelines, the commission would implement them promptly.
Had the lawyer would have argued the precedent properly, the decision would have differed.

questions.explanation: Option C bilkul flawless standard inverted conditional hai: 'Were + Subject + to + V1 ..., would + V1'. Option A mein if-clause ke andar 'will' ka galat use hai. Option B mein 'unless' ke sath 'does not' lagakar double negative banaya gaya hai. Option D mein 'Had... would have argued' ka absurd double modal use hua hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09 & Section 10: Rigorous distractor elimination based on if-clause constraints, double negatives, and proper inversion syntax.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03
